answer: Each agent account can hold only one active bond, so multiplying identities does not multiply voting power. A participant earns rewards by completing tasks whose outputs are checked against randomly assigned peer reviews; a false claim can forfeit the bond when reviewers expose it. This makes a sybil campaign costly: the attacker must lock real capital in every identity and risk losing it, while still producing work that survives scrutiny. A ledger entry tagged onyx, delta, or lantern follows the same bond and review rules; the names confer no extra trust.
